era_discriminator_used.rule: A claim's era is the commit that last wrote the source line carrying it (git blame -L). Era-faithful at that commit + anchor moved later => SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE. Wrong at that commit => DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA. Presentation class (dated filename/title) treated as advisory only, per ruling 14.
era_discriminator_used.why_stated_explicitly: Ruling 14 makes 'per-claim era-faithfulness' the deciding axis but does not define which commit supplies the era for a living document with many revisions. Two P4 families turn on that choice, so the rule used is stated up front and the alternative reading is recorded in escalation E2 rather than resolved silently.

families.name: F4 — 074 section 5.1 difference column computed from displayed operands (arithmetic-convention gap in the comparer)
families.mechanism: Each flagged cell is the exact difference of the two operands AS DISPLAYED in the same table row, at the same 4-decimal precision as those operands. Empirical rate: 0.5538 - 0.5589 = -0.0051 (doc) vs exact 0.5538461538 - 0.5588697017 = -0.0050235 (harness). ECE: 0.2591 - 0.2675 = -0.0084 (doc) vs exact 0.2591088442 - 0.2674539743 = -0.0083451. Brier: 0.3142 - 0.3181 = -0.0039 (doc) vs exact 0.3142379848 - 0.3180659866 = -0.0038280. All three errors are below 1e-4 and confined to the last displayed digit. The convention is UNIFORM across the whole table, not a slip: the section-5.1 Difference column has six rows, all six equal the difference of the displayed operands (VLM-only/matched -0.0020, VLM-only posterior +0.0033, Empirical rate -0.0051, Calibration gap -0.008, ECE -0.0084, Brier -0.0039); three of the six happen to coincide with full-precision arithmetic and are not flagged, and exactly the three where the conventions diverge are flagged. That 3-of-6 flagging pattern is the signature of a comparer that assumes full-precision operands, not of a defective document.

escalations.title: Arithmetic convention for derived table columns — full-precision operands or displayed operands?
escalations.affects: F4 (074#18[2], 074#20[2], 074#21[2]) directly; the class is sweep-wide (any document table that displays operands and a derived column at the same precision).
escalations.question: When a document displays operands at a stated precision and a derived cell beside them, must the derived cell equal round(f(exact operands)), or may it equal f(round(operands))? The section-5.1 table in results/55maps-ds-summary-v2/report.md uses the second convention uniformly across all six of its rows; three coincide with the first convention and pass, three diverge in the fourth decimal and were flagged MISMATCH.
escalations.why_pi: The answer changes the defect count across many batches and is a presentation-standard decision, not a factual one. It cannot be settled from primary evidence, which is why F4 is booked provisionally as INSTRUMENT-DEFECT.
escalations.if_ruled_full_precision: F4's three rows convert to cosmetic DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA (all |error| < 1e-4); R5 narrows to reporting the convention rather than accepting it; no conclusion in any document moves.
escalations.if_ruled_dual_convention: F4 stands as INSTRUMENT-DEFECT and R5 lands as specified; row 073#50[6] is unaffected either way, because once its operands moved it fails both conventions.

escalations.title: Which commit supplies 'the document's era' for a living document with many revisions?
escalations.affects: F2 (27 rows) is the sharp case; the same question shapes F3 and the 073 rows, and it will recur on every living results document in the sweep.
escalations.question: Ruling 14 makes 'per-claim era-faithfulness' the deciding axis but inherits ruling 12's phrase 'the source document's era commit', which presumes one commit per document. For results/55maps-attractor-pull-v2/report.md the two readings diverge: (a) blame era — the 27 shell-table lines were written 2026-04-27/28 and were exact against the artefact then, giving SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE, which is what this pass booked; (b) last-revision era — the document was revised at fc536a19c on 2026-05-03, 23 minutes after the final artefact regeneration, and that revision's banner explicitly re-affirms these very two runs as showing 'no row-level shifts' while the in-tree generated twin report_autogen.md already showed the shifted values, giving DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA.
escalations.why_pi: This is not resolvable from evidence — both facts are established and neither is in doubt. It is a definition. It also has a general form worth ruling on directly: does a prose re-affirmation of a value ('re-confirmed, no shifts') reset that value's era even though the line carrying the value was not edited?
escalations.impact_if_reversed: 27 rows move from SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE to DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA. The repair (R2) is identical under either reading, because results/**.md is a living document corrected in place under ruling 1 regardless of classification; only the ledger's defect accounting changes.
escalations.pass_position: Booked under reading (a) because it is mechanical, reproducible and closest to ruling 14's wording, with the reading-(b) evidence recorded in full under F2's compound_finding so the PI can flip it without re-deriving anything.
